core: Political power, institutions, comparative democracy and political theory
International relations, conflict, war and political cooperation
Empirical political inquiry using qualitative and quantitative methods
Inequality, political identities, social movements and public justice
adjacent: International peace, borders and foreign-policy ethics
questions: How do democracies change under polarisation, populism and unequal power?
How can political institutions manage conflict and foster peace?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: International law sources, use of force, armed conflict, refugee/environmental law, self-determination and treaty politics. Strong interdisciplinary IR/legal contribution.
Fiscal/monetary policy, growth, crises and international trade. Meaningful economic institutions/policy context; not the full power-centred international political-economy discipline.
Law, society and justice with legal systems and case/trial work; institutional context and legal preparation, not empirical comparative politics by itself.
Sociological concepts, institutions, classical/colonial theory, race and gender. Social context for politics rather than political-science equivalence.

EU actors/institutions/decision rules, Navigating the EU source work and actual group research on legislative dossiers, interests and MEPs. Direct politics/research contribution; stronger project relationship than an EU-law substitution.

Actual qualitative design, data collection, analysis, dissemination and group study with positionality reflection. Substantive methods, correctly paired to current qualitative Methods I, not prospective Methods II.
Movement theory, Environmental Justice Atlas, feminism, anticolonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding. Genuine activism/movements inquiry.
Historical empires, theories of power and great-power rise/fall; substantive international power context, not a dedicated contemporary foreign-policy module.
EU legal institutions, citizenship and internal-market freedoms through cases/PBL. Genuine European integration/legal complement, not the same as a political group project.

OLS, GLS and instrumental variables, statistical tests, Monte Carlo/Stata and an empirical paper. Substantive advanced quantitative inquiry; economics examples do not replicate every political-science regression/project requirement.

Actual governance actors, interests, public opinion and policy enforcement, with food/water/energy/climate problem-based cases. Genuine applied political/governance substance, not merely an environmental label.
Comparative constitutional structures, separation of powers and legal constraints on government. Substantive domestic institutional lens, distinct from empirical democratisation research.
Micro/macro foundations, game theory, consumer/firm behaviour and output/inflation/financial markets. Direct economics foundation for the international political-economy response.
Social cognition, attitudes, groups and influence; useful behavioural context, not political behaviour research training alone.
Modernity, imperialism and social theory; complements political/social inequality, not a dedicated electoral/party course.
Theory-driven qualitative/quantitative comparative political analysis; institutions, democracy/autocracy, parties and backsliding. Direct defining political-science substance.
Framing, nudging, persuasion ethics and real community communication projects. Meaningful political communication lens, broader than politics and not a campaign-employment guarantee.
Western military history, strategy, technology and hegemony; meaningful historical conflict lens, not negotiation or conflict-transformation practice.
Normative theory, equality, poverty, climate/historical injustice and argumentative research essay. Genuine ethical reasoning, not political-practice equivalence.
Actual research design, sampling, descriptive/inferential statistics and group empirical project; substantive introductory empirical methods, not advanced political regression alone.
Actual classical-to-contemporary political theories, authority/power justification, empirical/normative comparison, essays and presentations. Direct political-theory foundation.
Conflict causation, violence, peacebuilding, structural/identity/colonial perspectives and travelling concepts. Direct conflict-studies substance; no military-history-as-peacebuilding claim.

IR theories applied to historic/contemporary cases, group presentation and UN Security Council simulation. Direct IR foundation; incidental South China Sea reference does not establish the dedicated Indo-Pacific module.

Actual civil society, Gramsci/Habermas/Fraser, solidarity/migration and CEL observation of an NGO/CSO. Substantive civil-society research; not a full identity omnibus or the electoral regression project.
Human-rights treaties, monitoring, case law and philosophical/historical rights arguments. Genuine political justice/legal content, not full political science.
Classical rhetoric, argument, academic writing and speaking. Real communication skills; does not substitute the whole political-science academic-skills research module.

Actual international research and evidence-based youth resilience/radicalisation work, democratic school culture and civic engagement. Genuine political-violence prevention research contribution; not a teacher qualification.

alternatives.label: Political institutions, democracy and social change
alternatives.concept: A substantive interdisciplinary political-science response: comparative institutions and political thought, EU politics with group research, conflict studies, constitutional and international law, civil-society and movement inquiry, and introductory, qualitative and advanced quantitative methods. It remains broader than the Radboud route and does not reproduce all three political-science projects or its thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual comparative/theoretical/EU politics plus constitutional institutions, civil society, movements and persuasion sustain the institutions and social-change focus.

alternatives.label: International relations, conflict and peace
alternatives.concept: An international response retains the direct politics core while adding military/imperial history, international and human-rights law, youth radicalisation research, introductory economics and international macroeconomics. Qualitative research and econometrics support inquiry. It does not reproduce a dedicated Indo-Pacific module, the full political-economy discipline or Radboud’s three projects and thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: War and imperial history, international law, radicalisation research and15ECeconomics sustain a different international focus.
alternatives.distinctness: Exactly four different courses per programme,30EC: economics, international macroeconomics, war history and youth radicalisation replace modern sociology, comparative constitutional law, rhetorical skills and persuasive communication. These form an international power/conflict/economic lens versus domestic institutions/civil-society/communication. All other20courses are shared, so the alternatives remain closely related.

candidates.label: International relations, conflict and peace
candidates.assessment: Retained after replacing general philosophy/criminal-law emphasis with15ECeconomics and adding econometrics to both programmes; sustained international law/history/violence/economic perspective, exactly30ECdifferent from main.

routeSelection.basis: The target is generic Politicologie. Current OER has a complete earlier-cohort curriculum but only the new first year for2026 entrants. Select the complete2025cohort and first-listed Macht en Democratie branch neutrally before UCR comparison; disclose the route and retain open24ECchoice. Do not stack the alternative Macht en Conflict branch or prospective new years.

selection.assessment: Two qualified responses retained after actual content/weight review and feasible bounded correction. Exactly fourcourse/30ECfloor plus coherent qualitative distinction confirmed. A third democracy/justice/theory route would rearrange the same politics/law/sociology core. PublicPolicyAnalysis has no listed offering in the actual workbook, so cannot be used to force another route. No professional-equivalence/admission promise.

blocks: Political study, research and academic choice
Academic source work, questions, writing and civic reflection offer a foundation; Radboud adds a specific political research and language-assessment sequence.
Direct comparative political institutions, democratic change and political-science concepts provide a substantive foundation.
Classical and contemporary political thinkers and the justification of authority provide direct political-theory study.
Research design, operationalisation, sampling, statistics and a group project provide related empirical foundations across disciplines.
IR theories, international cooperation and a Security Council simulation provide related institutional and international inquiry.
Qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and a group study relate to qualitative political methods, with a sociological context.
Conflict causation, violence and peacebuilding provide substantive conflict inquiry at a more advanced interdisciplinary level.
Ethical theories and applied argumentative research contribute normative reasoning; political practice remains a different focus.
EU decision-making and an actual group investigation of legislative dossiers, interests and MEPs offer a substantive political research connection; project scope differs.
Civil-society theory and actual community organisation research provide a partial research connection, rather than the target’s democracy-and-representation project.
Persuasion, framing, ethics and community communication projects provide a related applied communication lens extending beyond politics.
EU institutions and legal foundations contribute a legal perspective on integration, rather than its complete political history.
Regression estimators, statistical testing, Stata and an empirical paper provide advanced quantitative inquiry. The target also requires logistic regression and direct political project application.
Introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics provide related economic foundations; the political-science context differs.
Fiscal and monetary policy, growth, crises and trade provide an economic lens; power-centred international political economy is broader.

notes.text: UCR provides substantial comparative politics, political theory, international relations, peace and conflict, EU politics and law, civil-society research and empirical methods. Radboud’s selected cohort has three dedicated political-science projects and a 12 EC individual thesis. Econometrics and related projects strengthen inquiry without replacing that whole discipline-specific sequence. Credits, qualifications and postgraduate admission are not equivalent.

audience.programmeDescription: Political Science at Radboud examines power, political institutions, justice, conflict and international relations. It combines political theory and comparative politics with qualitative and quantitative research, supervised projects and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two UCR programmes offer related study in political institutions and social change, or international relations and conflict. Both include direct political-science courses, law, sociology and empirical methods. The international programme adds economics, war history and radicalisation research. Neither reproduces Radboud’s complete political research-project sequence, dedicated Indo-Pacific course or individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: This is the complete 180 EC framework for students who entered before 2026, using the first-listed Power and Democracy route: 156 EC required study and 24 EC open choice. It includes three research projects and a 12 EC thesis. The redesigned first year for 2026 entrants is not combined with earlier-cohort later years. An internship is optional within the 24 EC choice space. Mandatory academic-language testing and participation add no credits. First-year progression normally requires 42 EC. UCR schedules illustrate a separate 2026-start programme, not Radboud’s calendar.
